results.name: Lord Hanuman Gada (mace)
results.description:
This is a 3D model of the sacred Gada (mace), the eternal weapon of Lord Hanuman, symbolizing unmatched strength, devotion, and protection.

In Hindu mythology, the Gada is more than a weapon – it represents power, courage, and righteousness. Lord Hanuman, the devoted bhakt of Shree Ram, carried this mighty mace as a sign of his divine authority and unshakable faith.

Legends describe the Gada as capable of destroying evil forces, shattering mountains, and protecting the righteous. It is not just a tool of battle, but a reminder of Bhakti (devotion) and Shakti (power).

This 3D recreation captures the timeless spiritual and mythological essence of Hanuman Ji’s weapon, bringing ancient symbolism into the digital era.

results.name: Relief of Khabekhnet (W927)
results.description: Painted limestone relief depicting Khabekhnet and his wife Sahte (to the right) presenting offerings to the gods Ptah (painted green), Ptah-Sokar (wearing a headdress consisting of ram horns and double plumes), and Isis (holding a menat-collar and ankh). Both Ptah and Ptah-Sokar hold long papyrus stems. Several enthroned deities are also depicted in the scene above, although only their feet are preserved. Khabekhnet is identified in the hieroglyphs as the “Servant of the Lord of the Two Lands”. The exact provenance of this relief is unknown, although it is likely from a tomb chapel at Deir el-Medina where Khabekhnet was buried (TT 2). Khabekhnet was the eldest son of Sennedjem, whose well-known tomb (TT 1) at Deir el-Medina was discovered undisturbed in 1886. While Ptah was the main deity at Memphis, he was also the patron god to the villagers of Deir el-Medina. The relief was purchased by Sir Henry Wellcome in 1906 from the collection of Robert de Rustafjaell (lot 404).

results.name: Monster Truck
results.description:
Monster truck 

A monster truck is a massive, heavily modified pickup truck or SUV designed for off-road and stunt performances. These vehicles feature oversized tires, high ground clearance, and reinforced suspension systems, allowing them to crush smaller cars, jump over ramps, and navigate extreme terrain. Monster trucks are commonly used in competitive events, such as freestyle stunt shows and races, where they perform gravity-defying tricks like wheelies, flips, and long jumps. With their loud, roaring engines and eye-catching custom designs, monster trucks are a thrilling spectacle for motorsports enthusiasts.
